title: Comparing Virtual Reality, Hypnosis, and Their Combination for Experimental Pain Modulation
official: Comparison of the Effects of Virtual Reality, Hypnosis, and Their Combination on Experimental Pain, Physiological Measures, and Electroencephalographic Signatures
summary:
This study looks at three ways to help manage pain without medication: virtual reality (using a VR headset to create an immersive distraction), hypnosis (using guided relaxation and suggestion), and a combination of both. Researchers want to know which approach - or combination - works best at reducing pain and discomfort.

Forty healthy adults will take part in a single research visit lasting about 140 minutes. During the visit, participants will experience mild, controlled pain from a small electrical stimulation on the ankle, adjusted to a level they can tolerate. They will try all three approaches (virtual reality, hypnosis, and the combination) during the same visit, in a random order. Throughout the visit, researchers will record how much pain and discomfort participants feel, along with body signals such as heart rate, breathing, skin response, and brain activity (using a comfortable EEG cap with no needles).

The goal is to better understand how these non-drug approaches work and whether combining them provides more relief than using either one alone. This research may help improve pain management for people undergoing medical procedures in the future.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18 to 35 years
* Fluency in French (validated French-language versions of all instruments and the hypnotic script)
* Capacity to provide free and informed consent
* Good general health, without uncontrolled acute or chronic pathology
* Sufficient visual and auditory acuity (corrected as needed) to interact with the experimental equipment (VR headset, hypnotic instructions)

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of major neurological disorders (epilepsy, severe head trauma, multiple sclerosis) or major psychiatric disorders (psychosis, dissociative disorders, active post-traumatic stress disorder)
* Current use of medication likely to affect pain perception or central nervous system activity (opioids, benzodiazepines, anticonvulsants, tricyclic antidepressants, gabapentinoids)
* Alcohol or psychoactive substance use within 24 hours prior to the session
* Use of analgesics (e.g., ibuprofen, acetaminophen, aspirin) within 24 hours prior to the session
* Contraindications to virtual reality (severe history of cybersickness, vestibular disorders, ophthalmic migraine)
* Contraindications to EEG recording (scalp lesions, incompatible cranial metal implants)
* Current or suspected pregnancy
* Skin lesions, peripheral neuropathy, or any condition preventing safe electrical stimulation of the sural nerve
* Inability to tolerate moderate painful stimulation during calibration, operationalized as: (i) inability to reach the RIII reflex threshold without exceeding a subjective intensity of 7/10, or (ii) explicit request to stop during the first three calibration steps
